fullPassage: The International Space Station, or ISS, is the ninth space station to be inhabited by humans. Since 2000, it has been continuously occupied by astronauts. It serves as a research laboratory for many fields, including astronomy, physics, and medicine. It is also used to test spacecraft systems required for possible future missions to the moon, Mars, and asteroids. As big as a football field, it is composed of many different sections, such as experiment modules, habitation modules, solar battery panels, and robotic arms. It is a completely unique structure assembled by spacewalkers flying around Earth at 28,000 kilometers per hour in a vacuum in extremes of temperature of plus and minus 270 degrees Celsius. It is the result of work by 15 different nations over about two decades. The work was carried out by thousands of people speaking different languages and using different engineering methods and standards. Putting the space station into orbit, making it work, and keeping it working are perhaps some of the most difficult things that human beings have ever done. In January 2022, NASA announced a plan to de-orbit the ISS in 2030. Many astronauts believe that it will stand forever as proof that when humans work together, we can do anything from going to Mars to solving our problems here on Earth.
